name: UGC 3960 (Hubble)
blurb: UGC 3960, a slowly rotating early-type galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: ugc3960-hubble
story: UGC 3960 is a slow rotator, its stars moving without the regular rotation of a disk. Hubble's sharp view found no flattened core at its center, a hint that gas helped build it.

claims.text: UGC 3960 is one of the 12 slowly rotating early-type galaxies (ATLAS3D slow rotators) imaged by HST program GO-13324
UGC 3960 was targeted as a low angular momentum early-type galaxy

Hubble imaging showed the 12 newly imaged slow rotators, including UGC 3960, have core-less central light profiles, consistent with formation through accretion of counter-rotating gas or gas-rich mergers
UGC 03960 is classified as a non-regular rotator
